title: Responder patterns and game-day catalog
author: Maya Chen
content:
Overview

This document describes the responder operational patterns used at Redwood Inference and a catalog of game-day exercises designed to validate on-call processes, runbooks, and customer communications. It combines: severity classification, a step-by-step triage and containment ladder, a set of reusable runbook templates, status page and customer-notice templates, on-call rotation guidance, and a prioritized game-day catalog tied to specific learning objectives.

Intended audience
- Primary: SREs, on-call engineers, service owners
- Secondary: Support, Customer Success, Product Reliability Partners

Scope
- Applies to all public-facing inference endpoints and the control plane services that impact customer request routing and billing.
- Excludes purely research/backfill batch jobs (see eng-infra runbooks for batch).

Key principles
- Restore customer-visible service first, investigate root cause later.
- Use observable, reproducible steps in runbooks; prefer deterministic mitigations over speculative changes.
- Communicate early and often: internal updates every 15 minutes during active incidents; public status every 30–60 minutes if customers impacted.

Severity classification (quick reference)
| Severity | Symptoms | Customer impact | Initial response SLA | Ownership |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|
| Sev 0 (SEV0) | Total region outage or control plane down (auth/billing) | All customers in region cannot use inference | 0–5 min acknowledge, 10 min mitigation start | Incident Commander (IC), Eng-SRE, On-call product owner |
| Sev 1 (SEV1) | Significant service degradation (>50% error rate or 3x latency SLO) | Major customer impact, potential SLA violations | 0–10 min acknowledge, 15 min mitigation start | IC, owning service team, Eng-SRE |
| Sev 2 (SEV2) | Partial degradation (single model pool or dedicated capacity) | Some customers affected, degraded performance | 15–30 min acknowledge, 1 hr mitigation plan | Owning service team, Eng-SRE |
| Sev 3 (SEV3) | Non-urgent issues (scheduled job failures, minor API errors) | Limited or no customer-visible impact | 1 business day triage | Owning team |

Incident lifecycle: step-by-step checklist
1) Alerting & Triage
   - On-call receives alert (PagerDuty / Opsgenie). Immediately ACK and open the incident in the incident tracker (Jira incident template).
   - Post basic context to #ops-incident (Slack): service, region, pager link, observed symptoms, metric snapshot.
2) Initial assessment (first 10 minutes for SEV0/SEV1)
   - Confirm alert: check Prometheus/Grafana dashboards, tail logs, and check service health endpoints.
   - Determine scope: single host / pool / region / control plane.
   - Assign roles: Incident Commander (IC), Primary Engineer, Communications Lead, Triage SRE. Use the incident roles checklist below.
3) Containment & Mitigation
   - Follow the owning service runbook. If none exists, use the generic containment ladder (below).
   - Apply short-lived mitigations only (traffic reroute, scale up, model fallback, circuit breaker). Record all actions.
4) Communication
   - Internal: IC posts cadence updates every 15 minutes to #ops-incident and /incident Zoom bridge.
   - External: Communications Lead drafts a status page entry and customer email draft (templates below). Publish first public update within 30–60 minutes if customer impact.
5) Recovery & Validation
   - Validate traffic restored using synthetic checks and customer-facing metrics. Confirm SLOs trending back to normal.
6) Post-incident
   - If Sev1/Sev0, create postmortem within 72 hours; complete and publish remediation plan within 14 calendar days.

Incident roles and responsibilities (cheat sheet)
- Incident Commander (IC): overall coordination, declares severity, approves customer comms, escalates.
- Primary Engineer: leads technical investigation and mitigation.
- Triage SRE: monitors observability, extracts logs/spans, renders dashboards for the IC.
- Communications Lead: writes status page copy, drafts customer emails, coordinates with CS and legal when necessary.
- Artifact Owner: ensures postmortem and follow-up actions are tracked to completion.

Generic containment ladder (use in runbooks when fast mitigation needed)
1. Verify and gather evidence (metrics, logs, spans).
2. Isolate noisy actor: disable host, cordon node, or remove from load balancer.
3. Fallback to compatible model or cheaper mode (e.g., shorter max_tokens / reduced beam) if available.
4. Scale up: add more workers to the pool or enable burst capacity lanes.
5. Route traffic to alternate region if cross-region resilience available.
6. Enable read-only mode or degrade non-essential features when all else fails.

Reusable runbook template (copyable)
- Title: <service> critical path runbook
- Purpose: One-sentence description of what this runbook restores.
- Who owns it: <team>, on-call rotation, pager alias.
- Runbook steps (ordered):
  1) Verify alert and collect coroners (logs/metrics).
  2) Validate impact using synthetic check: curl https://health.redwood.ai/<service>/healthz
  3) Common mitigations (exact CLI commands / playbook entries). Example:
     - kubectl -n inference get pods -l app=<service> --wide
     - coin assign rollback: terraform apply -target=module.<service>.replica_count=5
  4) Revert steps and validation commands.
- Escalation matrix and SLA targets.
- Post-incident checklist link and postmortem form link.

Status page / customer notice templates
- Status page short (first public entry):
  Title: [Incident] Increased error rates for <service> in <region>
  Impact: Customers may experience HTTP 5xx or increased latencies for requests routed to <service> in <region>.
  Current status: Investigating.
  Next update: <timestamp in UTC> or in 60 minutes.
  Link to workaround: <link> (if available)

- Customer email template (for high-severity incidents)
  Subject: Redwood Inference incident: <brief impact summary>
  Body: Hello <Customer name>
  We are investigating an issue affecting <service> in <region>. Impact: <brief>. What we are doing: <mitigations>. Expected next update: <time>. We will follow up with post-incident summary and remediation.
  -- Redwood Reliability Team

On-call rotation rules and handoff checklist
- Rotation length: 1 week primary + 1 week secondary (shadow).
- Coverage: 24/7 for SEV1/SEV0 teams; business-hours only for SEV3 services unless on-call roster indicates otherwise.
- Handoff items (Slack message + short Handoff ticket):
  - Current incidents and status
  - On-going mitigations or scheduled maintenance windows
  - Active alerts suppressed and reasoning
  - Local environment or access issues (VPN, KMS)
- Escalation frequencies: if an on-call does not ack within 5 minutes for SEV0 alerts escalate to secondary; if secondary does not ack within 10 minutes, escalate to Eng-SRE lead.

Game-day catalog: exercises and learning objectives
1) Exercise: Partial model-pool degradation (90m)
   - Scenario: Model serving pool in us-west-2 hits memory leak causing restart loop on 30% of serving workers.
   - Objectives: Validate containment ladder, model fallback, and customer notification cadence.
   - Success criteria: Traffic rerouted to fallback models within 20 minutes, status page update published within 30 minutes, no SLA breach for reserved capacity customers.
2) Exercise: Control-plane auth outage (120m)
   - Scenario: Auth service fails due to KMS misconfiguration preventing token validation.
   - Objectives: Validate cross-team coordination (SRE, Security, Product), verify customer token expiry handling, and practice legal/CS comms.
   - Success criteria: Partial recovery path documented, CS notified with draft email within 45 minutes.
3) Exercise: Multi-region latency spike (90m)
   - Scenario: Inter-region network flap increases tail latency to 5x in region-east.
   - Objectives: Validate routing policies, canary rollback, and synthetic traffic validation.
4) Exercise: Billing/control-plane performance regression (60m)
   - Scenario: New schema migration causes database slowdowns affecting billing queries and usage reporting.
   - Objectives: Validate prioritization (customer-facing inference kept online while control plane degraded), schedule safe rollback, and coordinate finance for customer invoice impact assessment.

Each exercise should include:
- Pre-req checklist (who to invite, which dashboards to snapshot, test customer accounts)
- Playbook copy to run during exercise (in a separate ephemeral Jira board)
- Post-game-day retro with concrete action items and owners

Postmortem and remediation cadence
- Template: Title, Summary (3-4 lines), Timeline (UTC), Impact, Root cause hypothesis, Contributing factors, Resolution and mitigations, Remediation plan with owners and ETA, Lessons learned, Detection & prevention checks added.
- Publish windows: Provide draft postmortem within 72 hours for SEV0/SEV1. Formal postmortem published within 14 days with remediation owner assignments.

Measurement and continuous improvement
- SLOs to track for on-call efficacy:
  - Mean time to acknowledge (MTTA): target < 5 minutes for SEV0/SEV1
  - Mean time to mitigate (MTTM): target < 30 minutes for SEV1
  - Postmortem completion rate: 100% for SEV0/SEV1 within 14 days
- Quarterly game-day schedule: each SRE and owning service to participate in at least one exercise per quarter.
- Runbook hygiene: each on-call team must review and sign-off runbook correctness every 6 months.

Appendix: quick reference commands and links
- Pager / on-call: https://pagerduty.com/redwood-inference (alias: @redwood-oncall)
- Incident tracker template: Jira project RED-INC (use template: "Incident - SEV")
- Useful commands:
  - kubectl -n inference rollout status deployment/<service> --watch
  - curl -sS https://health.redwood.ai/<service>/healthz | jq
  - redis-cli -h <host> -- raw "INFO" | grep used_memory
